strategy.summary: KMeans with lloyd or elkan and more clusters than distinct samples keeps relocating empty clusters to the origin each iteration, so inertia stays 0 and the loop never stops early (n_iter_ equals max_iter instead of 1). The fix relocates empty clusters to the biggest cluster in _average_centers and exits early when all samples sit at distance 0. Reproduce by building the buggy commit d43d7d61c159 from source and running the developer's test_relocating_with_duplicates, which should fail on the buggy build and pass on the fixed build.

system_packages: libopenblas (OpenBLAS 0.3.21 or 0.3.23 as reported in issue #28055)
a C/C++ compiler with OpenMP support (vcomp on Windows or libgomp on Linux)
build_commands: pip install -r build_tools/requirements or pip install numpy scipy joblib threadpoolctl pytest Cython
pinned_because: NumPy >= 1.19.5 and SciPy >= 1.6.0 are documented in README.rst as explicit, numerically relevant minimums, so they are the floor I rely on.
pandas >= 1.1.5 is documented as explicit and numerically relevant to the test data containers, so I rely on it as a floor.

Cython has no documented constraint (kind unbounded, issue #28055 only shows it as None), so I choose the latest Cython release compatible with the chosen NumPy and say so here; this is my choice, not evidence.

strategy.reproducing_test: test_relocating_with_duplicates (parametrized over algorithm in lloyd, elkan and array_constr over data_containers): X=[[0,0],[1,1],[1,1],[1,0],[0,1]], KMeans(n_clusters=5, init=X, algorithm=algorithm), expects ConvergenceWarning matching 'Number of distinct clusters \(4\) found smaller than n_clusters \(5\)' and asserts km.n_iter_ == 1.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision d43d7d61c159 the test fails: fit either does not emit the expected ConvergenceWarning or runs until max_iter so that km.n_iter_ != 1 (the assertion fails, or the run does not terminate at the default max_iter=300 path). On the fixed revision (the commit containing the _average_centers fix) all parametrized cases pass: the warning matches and n_iter_ == 1 for both lloyd and elkan.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare km.n_iter_ and the verbose iteration log for n_clusters=5 on the 5-distinct-point dataset: buggy shows n_iter_ at max_iter, fixed shows n_iter_ == 1.

input_output_examples.input: KMeans(n_clusters=6, init=init, random_state=0, verbose=True, algorithm='lloyd', max_iter=10_000).fit(X), X has 5 distinct points, init user-supplied
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Initialization complete; Iteration 0, inertia 40.0.; Iteration 1, inertia 0.0.; Iteration 2, inertia 0.0. ... continues with inertia 0.0 up to Iteration 299 at max_iter=300
input_output_examples.expected_output: Initialization complete; Iteration 0, inertia 40.0.; Iteration 1, inertia 0.0. (stops after Iteration 1)

risks: The defect depends on empty-cluster relocation firing every iteration; if the build uses a different relocation path, the buggy behaviour may not appear, so verify the buggy commit really lacks the fix before trusting the transition.

The test's data_containers parametrization includes sparse and pandas containers; if optional packages (pandas, scipy.sparse) are missing, those cases may skip or error rather than transition, so ensure they are installed.

The reproduction depends on OpenBLAS and OpenMP threading behaviour as reported in issue #28055; on a platform with a different BLAS or without OpenMP the floating-point path may differ and the defect may not manifest. This is not verified on other architectures or sanitisers.
The fixed-behaviour stopping criterion is inferred from the test's n_iter_ == 1 assertion and the commit message, not from an explicit tolerance value.
Cython version is not documented; the chosen version is my assumption and could affect the build of the buggy revision.
The PR date is blank, so the exact era of the codebase is not confirmed by evidence; the build must be done at the exact commit hash.

oracle.reference_source: developer test assertion km.n_iter_ == 1 and ConvergenceWarning message match
oracle.why: The transition is decided by an integer iteration count and a warning match, not by float values, so no numeric tolerance is needed.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, KMeans relocates empty clusters to the origin every iteration, so inertia stays 0.0 and the loop runs until max_iter. km.n_iter_ therefore equals max_iter rather than 1, so the assertion km.n_iter_ == 1 fails; the warning check may also fail depending on the path taken.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, empty clusters are relocated to the biggest cluster in _average_centers and the run exits once all samples are at distance 0, so n_iter_ == 1 and the ConvergenceWarning with 'Number of distinct clusters (4) found smaller than n_clusters (5)' is emitted for lloyd and elkan across all container types.
